rule.name: ReversedAssignableCheck
rule.message: The operands of this type test are reversed: type.isAssignableFrom(Foo.class) is true only when type is Foo or one of its supertypes, so every subclass of Foo is rejected, yet the code then casts a value to Foo as if the test had passed. Put the type of the value on the argument side: Foo.class.isAssignableFrom(type) (ClassUtils.isAssignable(Foo.class, type) in Spring), or test the value itself with value instanceof Foo or Foo.class.isInstance(value). A test that asks whether a Foo can be injected into a parameter of type type is right as written and has no cast after it.
